A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same IGDM research, with matching title, authors, central method and overlapping experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–C, which were inspected. Claims about newly documented details are limited to these supplied files.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original CIFAR-10/100 distillation experiments, adversarial accuracies, gradient and point-wise alignment measurements, training times and robustness analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and Tiny-ImageNet, alongside distribution-shift evaluations, controlled comparisons and hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: v1 Equation (8) uses adjustable inputs x+βδ and x−γδ, and Section 4.1 explicitly describes tuning these offsets. v2 Equation (8) specializes the loss to symmetric x±δ and tunes only α. The underlying output-difference matching procedure remains intact. Increasing T(α) weighting is retained in v2 Appendix B.2 and Algorithm 1, despite its simplified main-text formulation.

E1.justification: Coverage expands beyond CIFAR-10/100 to SVHN and Tiny-ImageNet, adding digit classification and a broader image-classification benchmark. v2 Table 9 also evaluates natural and corruption shifts through OODRobustBench, together with threat shifts including Recolor and StAdv. These introduce materially different data and input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated AKD and AdaIAD comparators to retained CIFAR comparisons; AKD's underlying work was only cited in v1. Appendices A.4–A.5 additionally compare IGDM against direct gradient matching, ARD plus TRADES regularization, and a zero-teacher-difference variant. These substantially expand the comparison set beyond v1's PGD-AT, TRADES, ARD, IAD, RSLAD and AdaAD.

E3.justification: v2 adds FGSM and C&W evaluation, OODRobustBench's dataset/threat-shift protocol, memory measurements, and an AdaAD replication using the larger WideResNet-34-20 LTD2 teacher. New dataset experiments introduce additional model configurations and training protocols. The retained PGD evaluation still uses 20 steps and an L-infinity bound of 8/255; newly disclosed CIFAR training details do not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct-versus-indirect matching controls and optimization traces, teacher-logit-difference controls, IGDM and AdaAD hyperparameter sweeps, a teacher-strength analysis, and distribution-shift tests. The teacher-free inner-maximization analysis expands to additional teachers and memory measurements. Conversely, v1's separately reported PGD-L1/PGD-L2, VMI-FGSM and larger-perturbation-bound analyses are no longer presented.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds numerical correlation coefficients, 0.895 and −0.837, to the gradient-alignment versus robustness analysis that v1 Figure 4 presented through scatterplots and regression lines. This is a limited addition to statistical reporting. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Extensive new results accompany the added datasets, comparators and controls. Retained CIFAR-100/BDM-AT entries also change: ResNet-18 IGDM_ARD AutoAttack accuracy changes from 29.42% to 28.79% in Table 2, and MobileNetV2 IGDM_RSLAD changes from 29.52% to 29.32% between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 10. ResNet-18 IGDM_AdaAD retains 30.32%. Some earlier result blocks and attack analyses disappear. These are revised reported results, without evidence establishing identical training conditions across versions.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 explicitly conditions the gradient-alignment argument on perturbation vectors varying during optimization and says minimizing the loss encourages alignment, qualifying v1's more direct inference from matching directional projections. The Taylor-expansion reasoning remains. The point-wise bound moves into Section 4.2, where its explicit approximation step is omitted; no substantial new proof or theorem is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain indirect gradient distillation using local linearity, compatibility with existing adversarial distillation methods, improved teacher–student alignment and enhanced robustness. The teacher-free inner-maximization efficiency claim remains in Section 4.3. Broader supporting experiments and revised headline numbers do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanation of why indirect matching helps. Appendix A.4 attributes direct matching's optimization difficulties to low-level gradient features; A.5 argues that teacher logit differences convey useful information beyond smoothing; A.6 identifies diminishing or adverse effects from excessive α. Section 4.3 also argues that adjusting AdaAD's two-point distillation balance cannot reproduce effective gradient alignment.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C supply optimizer parameters, epoch budgets, learning-rate schedules, inner-attack settings and losses, per-configuration α values, grid-search information, an explicit linear T(α) schedule and pseudocode. v1 largely refers readers to supplementary details absent from the supplied PDF. These are substantial documentation additions, not proof of changed execution. v1's prospective code-release statement is removed without a replacement code link.

R1.justification: v2 extends the retained research positioning with Sobolev training, perceptually aligned input-gradient literature, newer adversarial-distillation papers, and discussion of Chan et al.'s gradient-based robustness transfer using a discriminator. References supporting the removed transfer-attack experiments disappear. These refine the context while preserving the central distinction between direct gradient computation and IGDM's indirect approach.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: point-wise alignment moves from the method section into results, gradient alignment receives a separate results discussion, and AdaAD comparisons form an expanded dedicated subsection. MobileNetV2 and IKL-AT results move into appendices alongside new analyses and implementation sections. Method explanations and related-work prose are also revised beyond routine copyediting.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a predominantly single-column conference layout and redistributes v1's large comparison tables across main-text and appendix tables. Figure 1 gains a performance panel; the method flow diagram is removed; correlation plots are rearranged and annotated; and teacher-strength and optimization plots are added. Tables gain new comparator rows, attack columns and memory measurements, while the earlier large-bound attack figure disappears.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential and reproducibility gaps: Appendices A.4–A.6 test whether indirect matching and teacher differences matter, Section 4.3 strengthens baseline controls, and Appendix B documents the training recipe. SVHN, Tiny-ImageNet and distribution-shift evaluations substantially broaden validation. These gains outweigh the loss of specific earlier robustness tests. Remaining weaknesses include absent run-to-run uncertainty and unexplained numerical inconsistencies, such as IGDM_ARD clean accuracy of 61.62% in Table 2 versus 61.18% at the selected α in Table 18.
